APPLICATION OF Minnie Blair FOR THE ENROLLMENT OF Harry Blair IN THE INDIAN SCHOOL AT Tacoma, Wa POST-OFFICE ADDRESS OF APPLICANT: Polier, Mont Date of enrollment, ____________________________, 19 Term of enrollment, ____________________ (______) years. NAME OF PERSON ARRANGING FOR THE TRANSFER: Position, ____________________________________ APPLICATION FOR ENROLLMENT IN A NONRESERVATION SCHOOL. (For a child not enrolled at an Agency.) For and in consideration of the United States assuming the care, education, and maintenance in the United States Indian School at Lacawac, Pa., of Harry Blair, Male, 15, I, Minnie Blair, of their home P.O., State of Mont., do hereby voluntarily consent and agree to his enrollment in said school for a period of three years, and also obligate and bind myself to abide by all the rules and regulations for Indian schools. I further say that the said child was born at Blackfoot, Idaho, on Nov 24, 1903, that the father, George Blair, White, Indian of the Tribe located at Blackfoot Agency; that he left the tribe about [approximate date], that the mother, Minnie Blair, a [approximate date] Indian of the Tribe located at Blackfoot Agency, and left the tribe about [approximate date]; that the said child was born and reared in the United States, and now actually resides therein; and that he has attended the following schools:

Should the child be returned home for one of the vacation periods of this enrollment at my request I further agree to pay all expenses, including round-trip railroad fares, sleeping-car fares, meals, lodging, stage fares, telegraph and telephone messages, and other incidental expenses connected with the visit. I further agree that said pupil shall be returned to the school on or before the last day of the vacation period above named. I further agree to deposit with the superintendent of the school sufficient money to defray all expenses to be incurred, and should the child fail to return to school at such time as may have been agreed upon by myself and the superintendent of the school, the amount of money remaining with the superintendent, necessary to the return transportation of the child so neglecting to return, shall be forfeited to the Government. This 6th day of Sept., 1918 Two witnesses: John H. Henshaw Lucy McKnight P.O., Colmen Mont. The law provides: "That no part of this appropriation, or any other appropriation provided for herein except appropriations made pursuant to treaties, shall be used to educate children of less than one-fourth Indian blood whose parents are citizens of the United States and of the State wherein they live and where there are adequate free-school facilities provided and the facilities of the Indian schools are needed for pupils of more than one-fourth Indian blood." EXTRACTS FROM SCHOOL RULES. If the facilities of a school are not needed as provided in the above paragraph, children showing any Indian blood, whose parents live on an Indian reservation, and who if debarred from Government schools could not obtain an education, may be enrolled in the day and boarding schools of their reservation; these children, however, may not be transferred to nonreservation schools without special permission from the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Before enrolling a pupil superintendents must satisfy themselves whether he has left any other school without permission and whether he has been expelled for cause from any other school. A pupil who has been expelled for cause from any Indian school may be reenrolled in any Indian school only with permission of the Commissioner of Indian Affairs. Attention is invited to Circulars Nos. 1039 and 1044, which must be observed. "The Secretary of the Interior may in his discretion withhold rations, clothing, and other annuities from Indian parents or guardians who refuse or neglect to send or keep their children of proper school age in some school during a reasonable portion of each year." (27 Stat. L., 635. See 2 Dec. Comp., 308.) Elbowoods N. Dols. July 14, 1919. Sept. Hammond, Tacoma, Washington. Dear Sir: Could you not find or arrange some way so that Harry could go out to some good place during the remainder of this summer and work so he could earn something for himself? Altho he is not very bright in school I know he is good about work. Of course he has never done much of anything else but farm work. I'm positive there would be no danger of his running away. If you would please let him do this I would be very much obliged. Yours very truly, Mrs Minnie Blair. Supt Powell Brooming, Mont. WU South Bay phoned 11:35 A.M. Tacoma Wn Jan 6 - 1919 Mrs. George Blair wires husband dead Requests children sent home. No funds. If children can arrive in time for funeral wire me transportation. Hammond. Chq Cushman Ind. Sch. Title Lily Blair Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Wash., July 25, 1919 Mrs. Minnie Blair Elbowoods, North Dakota Dear Mrs. Blair: Harry has been going out to work every other day. Several days he has volunteered to help around the school but as a rule he has his every other day off to do as he pleases. He is looking better than usual. Lillian has been enjoying the whooping cough which we think she contracted about the time she returned, or shortly after her arrival. Otherwise, she is well. Sincerely yours, Superintendent. Cashman Indian School Confirmation of phoned message Jan 7-1919 The First National Bank Valier, Mont. Gentlemen: Pursuant to your telegram, I purchased two tickets for Harry and Lillie Blair at a cost of twenty dollars & fifty cents each ($20.50). We are not permitted to pay transportation of people home until the expiration of their all years enrollment. to me Please remit at your earliest convenience the sum of forty-one dollars to cover the cost of Harry Lillie's transportation. Please make check payable to J.O. McMullen, Agent, Federal Consolidated Ticket Office. As payment for the tickets has not been made, buy truly yours, Enclosure: (Copy of west un. telegram) Superintendent Ruth Kurt Union Jan 6-1919 Valier, Mont. At the request of Mrs. Geo Blair we will if necessary pay cost of transportation home for Harry & Louise Blair if they have not already left. Buy ticket to Browning Mont. where they will be met. wire answer First Natl Bank Received 3 P.M. TO OFFICER SENDING TELEGRAM. 1. Keep copy on this form for your files. 2. (Title of sender.) Tecoma, Wash. January 7, 1919 (Place.) (Date.) The Blair children left Seattle seven ten last night for Browning two weeks leave. Cushman Indian School, Tacoma, Wash. Nov. 13, 1918. Mr. George Blair, Valier, Montana. Dear Sir: Enclosed please find a letter from Harry. He had a rather serious attack of influenza, but thanks to careful nursing, did not contract pneumonia. Both he and Lillie are fully recovered, and I hope happy. It is suggested that you write to them often, bright, encouraging letters so that they may not be unduly troubled with homesickness. I remember how homesick I used to get when I first left home. Sincerely yours, Superintendent EMH-S REQUISITION Cushman Indian School Tacoma, Washington 191 The following articles are needed in my department.
